item.title: Former B.C. school trustee to challenge $750,000 penalty for anti-SOGI campaign
item.description: The lawyer for former Chilliwack, B.C., school trustee Barry Neufeld says he will be filing a court challenge against a ruling by the B.C. Human Rights Tribunal that he poisoned the workplaces of LGBTQ+ staff members with a public campaign against classroom resources on sexual orientation and gender identity.

item.title: Demonstrators march in Vancouver to mark four years since Russia’s invasion of Ukraine
item.description: Ukrainian flags and banners decorated the streets of Vancouver Sunday as demonstrators marched through downtown while singing the Ukrainian national anthem.

item.title: Canadian Union of Postal Workers set to vote on tentative deals in spring
item.description: OTTAWA — The Canadian Union of Postal Workers says its members will hold a ratification vote on tentative agreements with Canada Post between April 20 and May 30. item.title: Immigration Department helping Canadian military recruit foreign military members
item.description: HALIFAX — The head of Canadian Armed Forces says a policy aimed at attracting specialized foreign military members is getting a boost from the federal Immigration Department as the military scrambles to fill jobs amid a protracted personnel shortage. Gen. Jenni Carignan, chief of defence staff, says the military already has a program in place […]

item.title: New Westminster councillors push to keep Queensborough school bus on the road
item.description: Two New Westminster City councillors call for permanent provincial funding for the Queensborough school bus program, which is set to expire by the end of the current school year.

item.title: Relative of Tumbler Ridge shooter arrested, charged in Alberta
item.description: Jacob Van Rootselaar, who is related to Tumbler Ridge shooter Jesse Van Rootselaar, has been arrested in Alberta.

item.title: ‘If you’re not off the street, you may be shot’: B.C. tourist on chilling cartel warning amid violence in Mexico
item.description: Daily life is slowly returning to normal in parts of western Mexico, a day after cartel violence shut down highways, suspended flights and left Canadian tourists stranded and afraid.

item.title: New Westminster robbery renews warning on distraction thefts targetting seniors
item.description: An 88-year-old woman is recovering after she was violently robbed just steps from her home in Queensborough on the Family Day long weekend.

item.title: Vancouver mayor against ICE deployment during FIFA World Cup; councillors’ motion seeks confirmation from Ottawa
item.description: In a written statement, Vancouver’s mayor says that the United States’ Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is not welcome in the city during the FIFA World Cup.
